landing.headline: How tight is your boyfriend filter in Hong Kong?
landing.sub: You stack deal-breakers. We show how fast the pool vanishes. Sharp, dumb, honest.
landing.runsCounterHint: Live-ish counter is illustrative only — not an official statistic.
landing.recentEmpty: No saved runs yet. Finish a quiz and it lands here.
landing.disclaimer: Satire + statistics. Not a dating service. Not your therapist.
landing.heroBody: Stack age, height, income, district, education, flat, car, and lifestyle filters. We multiply public Hong Kong statistics (with a small correlation tweak) to show how brutal the joint odds are — and roughly how many men are left in the toy model.

landing.marqueeWithCount: ~{count, number} runs today (illustrative vibe counter) — HK stats × your filters — not therapy — not a matchmaker —
landing.process1Body: Walk through one screen per filter: must-have or don't care. No chat logs — just the deal-breakers you declare, saved locally until you calculate.
landing.process2Body: We combine Census 2021 shares, earnings percentiles, a height curve from the 2014/15 Population Health Survey, and blunt priors for flat and car — then multiply filters with a +12% correlation bump so tall + rich isn't astronomically worse than naive independence.
landing.process3Body: You get match odds (about 1 in N HK men), an estimated pool count, a delulu tier, and a breakdown of which filter cuts hardest — plus a shareable result if you want group chat judgment.
landing.specimensSub: Runs saved in this browser from the last few sessions. Tap one to reopen your filters and jump to the result.
landing.specimenQuote: "The objectivity of spreadsheets meets the tragedy of the heart."
landing.ctaClosingSub: Same city, same census tables — just fewer illusions about how many people pass every line you draw.
landing.footerLegal: © Delulu Lab HK — objectivity is a choice. Model outputs are illustrative, not predictions about any real person.

quiz.heightHint: Mean HK male height in government health stats is ~170 cm (2014/15 survey — still the clean published bundle we model from).
quiz.incomeHint: HK$100k+/mo is roughly top 2–3% of male earners.
quiz.flatHint: A harsh filter in Hong Kong. This means he owns his place (private), not family titled, not “we’ll figure it out later”.
quiz.carHint: Private car in HK is rarer than drama make it sound. Toy share in the model, not a BMW salesperson quote.
quiz.labMonthlyBand: Monthly threshold (HKD only — we're not pretending USD fixes your crush)
quiz.labDataSource: Sources: C&SD / CHP priors — toy model. Methodology page has receipts.

methodology.title: Methodology & sources
methodology.intro: Delulu Dating multiplies independent population filters. It's a Fermi estimate for dating — not a prediction about any individual human.
methodology.b1: Model: independent filters are multiplied (joint probability under independence). A +12% correlation uplift stops “tall + rich” stacks from being astronomically harsher than a naive model.
methodology.b2: Height: Census doesn't publish “mean male height” every year. We use the Population Health Survey (2014/15) male mean (169.5 cm) plus a literature SD (~5.8 cm) for the bell curve. Newer self-reported app polls inflate height — we keep the boring government curve until CHP publishes a replacement bundle.
methodology.b3: Income: Census and Statistics Department Annual Earnings and Hours Survey — male wage percentile curve (HK$), interpolated between published points.
methodology.b4: Age / marital / education: 2021 Census and thematic reports (simplified age-window and never-married proxies).
methodology.b5: Districts: 2021 Census district weights blended into male-share priors — illustrative, not block-level GPS accuracy.
methodology.b6: Smoking / kids: broad CHP / survey priors — rounded, not bespoke matchmaking intel.
methodology.b7: Flat and car use blunt priors on common deal-breakers. Must own flat keeps about 11% of modeled men. Must keep a car keeps about 24%. Not estate agency research.
methodology.outro: This is spicy satire plus public statistics. If you're offended, the numbers still love you. Probably.
